topic.seo_intro:
TP53, commonly known as the "guardian of the genome," is a tumor suppressor gene that plays a critical role in protecting cells from becoming cancerous. When functioning normally, the TP53 gene produces a protein that stops the growth of abnormal cells and triggers their destruction if they become damaged. However, TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancers, found in approximately 50% of all cancer cases across multiple types including breast, colorectal, lung, and ovarian cancers. Understanding TP53 mutations has become essential for cancer researchers and clinicians seeking to develop better diagnostic tools and targeted treatment strategies.

The study of TP53 as a biomarker has revolutionized how researchers approach cancer diagnostics and prognosis. TP53 mutations can serve as important indicators of cancer risk, disease progression, and potential treatment response. By analyzing TP53 status in tumors, oncologists can better understand the biological characteristics of a patient's cancer and make more informed decisions about therapy options. This genetic information has opened new pathways for personalized medicine approaches in cancer care, allowing for more precise and individualized treatment plans based on each patient's unique tumor profile.

On this page, you'll find comprehensive information about TP53 in cancer research, including its role as a diagnostic biomarker, recent clinical findings, and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting TP53-mutated cancers. The articles and research summaries below represent the latest peer-reviewed studies from leading cancer research institutions, providing evidence-based insights into how TP53 research is advancing our understanding and treatment of cancer.

articles.hook: In this study, we illustrated the significance of TP53 deletion (D) in systemic ALK-negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL), an area that remains unknown.

articles.title: Complex structural variations functionally inactivate the telomerase chaperone TCAB1 in osteosarcoma.
articles.hook: Structural mutations in osteosarcoma simultaneously disable TP53 and TCAB1, pushing cells toward alternative telomere lengthening pathway activation.
articles.summary: Structural mutations in osteosarcoma simultaneously disable TP53 and TCAB1, pushing cells toward alternative telomere lengthening pathway activation.

articles.title: ZNF662 inhibits oncogenesis through NUPR1/p53 signaling pathway in epithelial ovarian cancer and is regulated by hsa-miR-429.
articles.hook: ZNF662 inhibits ovarian cancer growth via NUPR1/p53 pathway activation
articles.summary: ZNF662 protein inhibits epithelial ovarian cancer growth by activating tumor-suppressing p53 pathways, controlled by a specific microRNA.

articles.title: TP53 mutation at codon 179 metabolically reprograms cancer cells to promote invasion.
articles.hook: TP53 codon 179 mutation increases prostate cancer cell invasion via lipid accumulation
articles.summary: TP53 mutations at codon 179 boost cancer cell invasion by reprogramming cells to accumulate more fats.

articles.title: Independent somatic TP53 mutations in blood and tumor mimicking Li-Fraumeni syndrome in a 94-year-old man.
articles.hook: Independent TP53 mutations in blood and tumor mimic inherited cancer syndrome
articles.summary: A 94-year-old man developed identical TP53 mutations independently in blood and tumor, mimicking inherited cancer syndrome but arising from separate somatic events.

articles.title: Single-cell analysis reveals an endothelial TP53-CXCL14 axis in breast cancer progression.
articles.hook: TP53-CXCL14 axis in endothelial cells drives breast cancer progression
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that a protein pathway involving TP53 and CXCL14 in blood vessel cells drives breast cancer progression.

articles.title: Interpreting TP53 variants: somatic mosaicism and ERCC6L2-driven clonal evolution.
articles.hook: TP53 somatic mosaicism affects cancer risk stratification accuracy
articles.summary: TP53 variants require careful interpretation considering patient age, phenotype, and tissue testing to avoid misdiagnosis and guide appropriate cancer surveillance.

articles.title: Homozygous TP53 alterations: a case of a biallelic splice variant and a brief review of the literature.
articles.hook: Homozygous TP53 splice variant causes aggressive choroid plexus carcinoma in infant
articles.summary: A rare homozygous TP53 mutation caused aggressive choroid plexus carcinoma in an infant, highlighting genetic testing importance in pediatric tumors.

articles.title: The biology of hypomorphic TP53 variants and implications for clinical management.
articles.hook: Hypomorphic TP53 variants delay cancer onset, require modified surveillance protocols
articles.summary: Weakened TP53 gene variants increase cancer risk later in life than classic cases, requiring tailored screening approaches.

articles.title: An integrative mutational and network analysis of pancreatic cancer reveals key genes, and signalling pathways.
articles.hook: KRAS and TP53 mutations predict pancreatic cancer prognosis through pathway analysis
articles.summary: Researchers identified six frequently mutated genes in pancreatic cancer, including KRAS and TP53, and mapped their interconnected signaling pathways for prognosis assessment.
